summary:
PlanetHunter is an interactive, public-facing astronomical exploration platform that transforms real NASA SPHEREx observations into dynamic visualizations of the changing infrared sky.

Users can enter celestial coordinates or select known astronomical targets to retrieve, align, and animate observations across multiple epochs. The platform enables users to explore stellar proper motion, brightness variations, and potential moving objects through an accessible web interface.

Beyond visualization, PlanetHunter introduces an experimental Discovery Lab that detects sources, associates observations across epochs, and fits physically motivated motion models incorporating annual parallax. This allows users to investigate candidate distant Solar System objects while understanding the uncertainties associated with astronomical discovery.

By combining NASA's open scientific data, computational astronomy, interactive visualization, and machine learning experiments, PlanetHunter makes astronomical exploration accessible to students, researchers, and citizen scientists.
details:
PlanetHunter

The Problem

The universe is constantly changing. Stars move, variable stars change brightness, and distant Solar System objects shift against the background sky. However, accessing and interpreting multi-epoch astronomical observations often requires specialized software, programming knowledge, and familiarity with scientific data formats.

NASA's SPHEREx mission provides an extraordinary opportunity to explore these changes through repeated infrared observations of the sky. PlanetHunter aims to make this valuable scientific resource accessible through an intuitive, interactive web application.

Our Solution

PlanetHunter retrieves real SPHEREx observations from the NASA/IPAC Infrared Science Archive (IRSA), processes scientific FITS images, and transforms them into interactive time-lapse visualizations.

Users can explore any supported sky region by entering Right Ascension and Declination, selecting a field of view, choosing a detector, and specifying the number of observational epochs.

The platform registers observations onto a common celestial coordinate grid, allowing users to compare images consistently and investigate changes over time.

Key Features

  • Interactive Sky Explorer: Retrieve real SPHEREx observations and visualize the same region of the sky across multiple dates.
  • Astronomical Target Presets: Explore Barnard's Star, Epsilon Indi B, WISE 0855, RW Aurigae, and R Draconis.
  • Astrometric Tracking: Predict target positions using proper motion and annual parallax.
  • Epoch Comparison: Compare observations, calculate difference images, and explore potential changes in source brightness.
  • Live Discovery Lab: Detect astronomical sources and investigate candidate moving-object trajectories using multi-epoch astrometry.
  • Physics-Based Ranking: Evaluate candidate trajectories using parallax fits, inferred distances, motion residuals, and approximate orbital-speed constraints.
  • Research Dashboard: Explore synthetic moving-object recovery experiments and machine learning ranking results.

Scientific Research

PlanetHunter goes beyond conventional astronomical visualization by implementing an experimental pipeline for investigating distant moving objects.

The pipeline detects sources in registered images, identifies persistent background objects, generates candidate associations across observational epochs, and evaluates stationary, linear-motion, and parallax-based models.

To investigate its performance, synthetic moving objects were injected into real SPHEREx backgrounds. Recovery experiments evaluated whether the injected sources could be detected and correctly associated across multiple observations.

In one experiment, a synthetic object injected at approximately 1,479 AU was recovered through a three-epoch trajectory with an inferred distance of approximately 1,484 AU. This demonstrates recovery under the assumptions of the simulation, rather than independent validation of real-world discovery accuracy.

Machine learning experiments also investigated whether a trained ranking model could improve candidate prioritization. Initial held-out simulation results showed comparable performance between machine learning and physics-based ranking, motivating further research rather than unsupported claims of improvement.

Technologies

Python, Streamlit, Astropy, Astroquery, NumPy, Pandas, SciPy, Reproject, Plotly, Scikit-learn, GitHub, and NASA/IPAC IRSA SPHEREx data services.

Scientific Limitations

PlanetHunter is an exploratory research prototype. Predicted target positions do not guarantee source detection, and candidate moving-object trajectories do not constitute confirmed planetary discoveries.

Differences in effective wavelength, instrumental conditions, source blending, and limited observational coverage can affect the interpretation of astronomical images.

The application communicates these limitations explicitly to encourage responsible scientific exploration.

Impact and Future Vision

PlanetHunter aims to reduce the technical barriers to astronomical discovery by making real infrared sky observations accessible through a browser.

Future developments could include wavelength-matched observations, uncertainty-aware trajectory fitting, additional astronomical catalogue cross-matching, improved source detection, and large-scale candidate searches.

Ultimately, PlanetHunter seeks to empower anyone to explore a changing universe and participate in the scientific process.


Github Repository of the Project: https://github.com/dishitagarwal22-cyber/PlanetHunter
